beats.say: Every document has a level: public, internal or confidential. The level tells you who may see it.
Public means anyone, like a notice on the website. Internal means staff only.
Confidential is for named people only. If it leaks, people and the organisation are seriously harmed.
A link open to anyone exposes the file to the whole internet. Share with named people and set an end date.

scenes.title: Sharing requests
scenes.intro: Three requests reached your phone. Decide by the document's level: do you share or not?

body.text: Hi! I need it at my new job: could you send me the internal phone book?

actions.label: It is internal, I cannot send it
actions.feedback: Correct. Internal documents are for staff only, and a former colleague is now an outsider.

actions.label: I send the file
actions.feedback: The phone book is internal. Outside, it is a ready list of phishing targets.

body.text: Hello, could you send the job advert from your website? We would like to share it with our students.

actions.label: I send the advert
actions.feedback: Correct. A job advert is public and already on the website.

actions.label: I send nothing
actions.feedback: Safe, but a public document needs no hiding. Sending the website link is enough.

messages.text: Hello, I am a journalist. If you send the list of citizen applications, we will never mention your name.

actions.label: I refuse and refer them to the press office
actions.feedback: Correct. Applications are confidential and only the press office talks to the media.

actions.label: I send the list
actions.feedback: A confidential list has left the organisation. This is a leak of citizens' personal data.

actions.label: Report
actions.feedback: Good. Report a request like this to the security team and your manager too.

scenes.prompt: Match each document with its level.

pairs.left: A job ad published on the website

scenes.explain: When in doubt, pick the higher level and ask the document's owner.

scenes.prompt: This email reached you by mistake. Find the sharing errors.

body.text: full list of citizen applications with ID codes
I also uploaded it to the cloud,
anyone with the link can open it.

spots.label: Wrong recipient
spots.explain: The email is written to Leyla but reached you. That is an autocomplete mistake.

spots.label: Too much data
spots.explain: The task did not need the full list with ID codes. Send only what is needed.

spots.label: Open link
spots.explain: A confidential file must never have an open link. Anyone who gets the link can open it.

spots.label: Password in the same email
spots.explain: A password in the same email as the file protects nothing. Send it by another channel.

scenes.prompt: You sent a confidential file to the wrong person. Put the steps in order.

items.label: Close the sharing link at once
Tell your manager and the security team
As they advise, ask the recipient to delete the file
Write down what went to whom and when

scenes.explain: Anyone can make this mistake. Reporting fast reduces the harm, hiding it makes it worse.

question.prompt: You are sending a project file to an external partner. Which setting is right?

options.label: Anyone with the link, no expiry
options.feedback: The link can be forwarded and anyone could open the file.

options.label: Only the named person, for 7 days
options.feedback: Correct. Access is narrow and time limited.

options.label: Upload to my personal cloud and send a link
options.feedback: A personal account is outside the organisation's control.

scenes.explain: Keep sharing as narrow as possible: who, for how long and with what rights.

points: Before sending, check the document's level and the recipient.
Limit links by name and time, send passwords separately.
If you sent it wrong, do not hide it, report at once.
